nodes.title: K-flat module complexes
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R and an integer cochain complex C of R-modules, IsKFlat(C) means that for every acyclic integer cochain complex E of R-modules the native direct-sum total complex E tensor_R C is acyclic. There is no boundedness or termwise-flatness hypothesis in the predicate. This is the native ModuleCat adapter for SmoothRep.IsKFlat at the trivial group; the upstream definition is the owner of the generic construction.
proofSteps: Use the existing acyclic predicate and the native signed direct-sum tensor complex; quantify over all complexes in one fixed module universe.
Transport the upstream predicate through SmoothRep R {1}≃ModuleCat R and the signed tensor comparison; prove the displayed all-acyclic-complex criterion agrees with the transported predicate.
acceptance: An acyclic complex of nonflat terms need not be K-flat.

nodes.title: Module specialization of the derived tensor bifunctor
nodes.statement: For every commutative ring R, derivedTensor is an additive bifunctor D(R)→(D(R)→D(R)) on the native derived category of ModuleCat R. Its value is Q(P tensor_R T) for unbounded K-flat replacements P of X and T of Y; morphisms descend from the homotopy category localization. Current upstream SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0d already owns the derived tensor at the trivial group; this node transports it to ModuleCat R and compares the native chain tensor and localization.
proofSteps: Use the trivial-group equivalence in current upstream SR.0d, its exact derived-category comparison and signed monoidal tensor–Hom structure. Transport the existing derived tensor bifunctor to the native module derived category. Compare with native localization and K-flat chain tensor representatives. No new generic derived operation is proposed.
acceptance: The output is an object of the actual D(R), with actual morphisms, rather than a family of homology modules.

nodes.statement: For every projective R-module P, there exist an index type I and countably generated projective R-modules P_i with an R-linear equivalence P≅directSum_i P_i. Neither R nor P is assumed Noetherian or finite.
proofSteps: Realize P as a retract of a free module. Close a countable set of basis indices under the finite supports of its images under the retract idempotent; this gives an invariant countable coordinate summand. Well-order the remaining basis, repeat on successive quotients, and take unions at limits. Split successor factors and identify their direct sum with P. The invariant-support recursion and transfinite direct-sum equivalence require the separately recorded refinement gap.
acceptance: Countable generation concerns each summand, not the whole module.

nodes.title: An element of a local projective module lies in a finite free summand
nodes.statement: If R is local, P is projective, and x belongs to P, there is a finite free direct summand N of P containing x.
proofSteps: Embed P as a direct summand of a free module F. Choose a basis of F minimizing the finite support of x. No coefficient of x lies in the ideal generated by the others. The finite matrix of the projection F→P on this support consequently has diagonal entries congruent to 1 and off-diagonal entries in the maximal ideal. Its determinant is a unit. The projected basis vectors therefore span a finite free summand of F, contained in P and containing x; restricting the retraction makes it a summand of P. The support-minimization/basis-change argument is recorded for further lemma refinement.
acceptance: The conclusion holds without finite generation of P.

nodes.title: Countably generated local projective modules are free
nodes.statement: A countably generated projective module over a local ring is free.
proofSteps: Enumerate generators. At each step split off a finite free summand containing the residual image of the next generator. The complement is projective, so local-free-summand applies again. The union of the finite partial sums contains every generator. Finite-support independence identifies the module with the direct sum of these finite free summands.
acceptance: The basis may be countably infinite.

proofSteps: Decompose into countably generated projective summands; choose a free basis on each by countable-local-projective-free. Their disjoint union is a basis of the direct sum.

nodes.title: Residue generators span across a nilpotent ideal
nodes.statement: If I is a nilpotent ideal of R and a family v_i in M spans M/IM over R/I, then the same family spans M over R. The index type and M may be infinite.
proofSteps: For N the span of the family, residue spanning says M=N+IM. Inductively M=N+I^k M. Choose I^k=0 to conclude M=N. Every module element has finite support in a span; no finite-generation form of Nakayama is used.
acceptance: This fails for a nonnilpotent maximal ideal: Q_p over Z_p has zero residue and is nonzero.

nodes.title: Arbitrary residue bases lift over an Artinian local ring
nodes.statement: Let R be local with nilpotent maximal ideal, and M flat. For any basis of M/mM and any lifts of its basis vectors, those lifts are a basis of M. In particular M is free with the same arbitrary rank.
proofSteps: The native flat-module lemma gives linear independence of the lifts. nilpotent-residue-spanning gives spanning, hence the canonical finite-support linear-combination map is a linear equivalence.

nodes.title: Residue lifts span every DVR quotient
nodes.statement: For a DVR O with uniformizer π, any O-module P and lifts x_i of a basis of P/πP, the images x_i span P/π^nP over O/π^n for every n≥1.
proofSteps: Apply nilpotent-residue-spanning to the image of (π) in O/(π^n), whose nth power is zero. Its residue quotient of P/(π^nP) is P/(πP).
acceptance: Torsion freeness is not required for spanning.

nodes.title: Torsion-free residue lifts are independent modulo powers
nodes.statement: If multiplication by π on P is injective, lifts x_i of a basis of P/πP are linearly independent in P/π^nP over O/π^n for every n≥1.
proofSteps: Induct on n. A finitely supported relation modulo π^(n+1) reduces modulo π to show each coefficient is divisible by π. Write coefficients πs_i and use injectivity of multiplication by π on P to cancel π in the relation. Induction shows all s_i divisible by π^n.
acceptance: Finite support of each relation is essential; arbitrary products are not substituted for the free module.

nodes.title: Torsion-free modules are free modulo uniformizer powers

proofSteps: Combine spanning and linear independence of the same lifted family to produce the basis.

nodes.title: Freeness lifts over a finite free coefficient algebra
nodes.statement: Let O be a DVR, n≥1, and S a finite free O-algebra. Let M be an S-module killed by π^n, free as an O/π^n-module. If M/πM is free over S/πS, lifts of any S/πS-basis form an S/π^nS-basis of M.
proofSteps: Choose an O-basis z_j of S and a residue S/πS-basis y_i of M/πM. The products z_j y_i form an O/π-basis of the residue module. Since M is O/π^n-free, nilpotent-flat-free shows their lifts form an O/π^n-basis of M. Expanding each S/π^n coefficient in the finite basis z_j proves independence and spanning of the y_i over S/π^n.
acceptance: S is not required to be local.

nodes.title: Finite bounded above cohomology is pseudo-coherent
nodes.statement: Over a Noetherian commutative ring R, an object X of D(R) is pseudo-coherent if and only if H^i(X) is finite for every i and H^i(X)=0 for i sufficiently large.
proofSteps: A bounded above finite free model has finite homology because submodules of finite modules are finite over a Noetherian ring. Conversely descend from the top nonzero cohomology degree, choose finite free generators, and attach them to the partial model. The cone retains finite cohomology by the long exact sequence and Noetherian closure under subquotients. Use the same descending attachment and union contract as mpseudo-all-orders-model.
acceptance: The Noetherian hypothesis is not removed.

nodes.title: Noetherian finite-cohomology perfectness criterion
nodes.statement: Over a Noetherian ring, X is perfect if and only if it has bounded finite cohomology and finite Tor-amplitude. Over a complete Noetherian local ring, a pseudo-coherent X with bounded residue-derived cohomology is perfect.
proofSteps: Combine finite-cohomology pseudo-coherence with perfect-pseudo-finite-tor. In the local case, minimal-support-amplitude replaces finite all-module Tor-amplitude by bounded derived residue cohomology.

nodes.title: Bounded complexes of complete flat modules
nodes.statement: For a complete Noetherian commutative local ring R with maximal ideal m, IsCompleteFlatComplex(C) means C is an integer cochain complex with a finite strict term-support interval, every C^i is flat over R, and every C^i is m-adically separated and complete. Maps are native R-linear chain maps; they are continuous for the adic topologies. Terms may have infinite rank.
proofSteps: Combine native flatness, native IsAdicComplete m, and strict finite term bounds. An R-linear map sends m^nM into m^nN, so is adically continuous.
acceptance: Ordinary algebraic completion is not a substitute for the derived-completeness predicate of DD.1.

nodes.title: Split a complete flat map into its invertible and residual-zero parts
nodes.statement: For R as above and an R-linear map f:M→N between flat m-adically complete modules, there exist decompositions M=M_1⊕M_2 and N=N_1⊕N_2 into complete flat summands such that f preserves the summands, f:M_1→N_1 is an isomorphism, and f:M_2→N_2 reduces to zero modulo m.
proofSteps: Choose a residue basis adapted to the kernel and image of the residue map and import the completed-direct-sum lifting theorem requested from PM:L0. Extend the image basis to the target. In topological bases, f has blocks identity,C,0,B, with columns tending to zero. Subtract the convergent C-block columns from the complementary domain basis to obtain identity,0,0,B. B has rows indexed by the target complement and columns by the source complement, with entries in m.

nodes.title: Cancel one complete flat contractible disk
nodes.statement: If a differential of a bounded complete flat complex C has an invertible block J in degree i→i+1, C is chain isomorphic to a direct sum N⊕Disk(J,i), where Disk has identity differential, N is complete flat, and the degree-i differential of N has residual zero on the retained complement.
proofSteps: After the block diagonal change from complete-flat-morphism-splitting, d²=0 forces adjacent differentials to avoid the invertible block. Projecting it out is a chain map, and the inverse identity block defines the contracting homotopy of the disk. This argument uses the block decomposition directly; the accepted rank-one unit-pivot calculation supplies the sign convention, not an infinite iteration of finite pivots.
acceptance: The canceled block may have infinite topological rank.

nodes.title: Minimal complete flat representative with a chain deformation retract
nodes.statement: For bounded complete flat C over R, construct noncanonically a complete flat complex N in the same term interval, with every differential zero modulo m, chain maps i:N→C and s:C→N satisfying i followed by s=id_N, and a chain homotopy from s followed by i to id_C. Thus both maps are quasi-isomorphisms. The construction chooses topological residue bases.
proofSteps: Cancel invertible blocks in ascending order through the finite support interval. Later cancellation does not destroy the residual-zero property already achieved: it restricts a residual-zero adjacent differential and conjugates by invertible changes of basis. Compose the finitely many deformation retracts.

nodes.statement: If complete flat C is supported in [a,b] and H^i(C tensor_R κ) is finite-dimensional for all i, Q(C) is perfect and has a finite free representative supported in [a,b].

nodes.title: Degree-zero dual of a nonnegative perfect model
nodes.statement: For a finite projective complex P supported in [0,l], H^0(perfectDual(QP)) is naturally coker((d^0)^*:Dual(P^1)→Dual(P^0)). For every ring map R→B its ordinary scalar extension identifies with the analogous cokernel of the termwise B-dual of B tensor_R P.

nodes.statement: For a Noetherian commutative ring R, ideal I, I-adically complete R and finite R-module M, M is I-adically complete and its canonical map to native AdicCompletion I M is a linear equivalence.
